sections.body: Course design and teaching is where AI is used to build curricula, write assessments, adapt learning paths, tutor students, and generate lecture materials. In practice, AI tools can map topics to learning outcomes, draft quiz questions, summarize readings, and produce slide outlines from notes. They can also flag students who may need support by looking at engagement and performance patterns. The work is not fully autonomous. Instructors still set goals, check accuracy, and decide what counts as learning. AI is mostly an assistant for drafting, organizing, and personalizing at scale.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Some parts are more mature than others, and generating multiple choice questions and lecture outlines from existing notes is common and often reliable enough for a first draft. Curriculum mapping and alignment to outcomes still need human review because AI can miss prerequisite structure and local context. Personalised learning and early warning systems can surface patterns, but they can also reflect bias in past data and may mistake correlation for cause. Course-Specific AI Tutors can answer questions and explain concepts, yet they may hallucinate or fail on nuanced feedback. The honest limit is that AI does not know a course's hidden standards, department politics, or a student's full situation. The site's library of 288 research papers can help check which teaching methods have evidence behind them.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The pages here follow a teaching workflow. Curriculum and Learning Outcomes sets the frame for what a course must cover and how success is defined. Generating Assessments takes that frame and turns it into quizzes, assignments, and rubrics. Personalised Learning and Early Warning looks at how students move through the material and where they may struggle. Course-Specific AI Tutors gives a conversational layer for questions inside the course. Lecture Materials from Notes helps turn raw instructor notes into slides, handouts, and explanations, and together they move from planning to delivery to support.
